stage1.impression: A calm, well-exposed night interior with a strong idea (a glowing ice-blue speaker against a wall of records), but it reads as a clean CG render rather than a photograph: the record sleeves are flat, uniform colour strips with no wear, print or variation, the floor and walls are smooth and textureless, and a wide dead band of plain wall separates the two halves of the frame. The speaker's cyan interior is the best thing in the image, but its horn sinks murkily into the wall and its light never reaches the floor, so it sits on the set rather than in the room.

blocking_9: The record wall must read as real vinyl: varied sleeve thickness, printed spines, worn and sun-faded edges, records leaning and part-pulled, no repeating stripe pattern
The frame must show what it is for: at least one lounge chair in the foreground, with the speaker and the record wall behind it, and no empty central wall band
The speaker's own cyan light has to show on the floor and on the plinth's top edge, so it is visibly lit from inside and sits in the room
The horn needs separating from the wall: a readable rim or back light on its silhouette, with its tint and depth visible rather than a dark smoky slab
The floor and walls need real micro-texture (honed concrete with aggregate, trowel marks, faint reflections; plaster with variation), not smooth CG planes
The record wall must not outshine the product: no clipped sleeve spines, and the speaker must be the brightest coloured element

defects.what: dead central band of plain wall, nearly flat (lum_range 65 over 1150 px tall, a smooth falloff with no texture or object), splits the composition in two
record sleeves are flat, saturated colour strips with no print, wear or thickness variation; the pattern repeats across cubbies; 1.45% of pixels clipped on the top-lit spines
the shelf columns jog up and down between columns (stepped horizontal shelves) and read as modelling misalignment
horn is murky and underlit (lum_median 34 against a wall of about 65); the driver behind it shows as a soft dark blur, and its top edge merges into the wall
dark plinth with no cyan bounce on its top face or on the floor around it; the floor beside it is neutral-warm (r 103, g 93, b 73), so the product looks placed, not glowing in the room
smooth, low-detail concrete floor (lum_range 21) with sparse speckles; reads as a CG plane
right-hand corner wall is flat and empty, with a soft gradient that looks like a studio sweep, not a room
the inner cyan batts have an even emissive look with little falloff through the acrylic; they read slightly as self-lit plastic

changes.problem: The frame does not show the lounge chairs it is meant to show, and the empty wall between the record wall and the speaker kills the composition.

evidence.measured: a plain wall band 440 px wide, lum_median 64.8, range 65, with no object; no chair anywhere in frame

change.to: position [14.2, 2.3, 1.0], target [17.6, 1.2, 0.85], 35 mm, f/2.8 focused on the speaker's front face; frame so that a lounge chair's back and arm come into the lower-left foreground, softly out of focus, with the speaker on the right third and the record wall behind the chair

changes.expected: foreground (chair), middle ground (speaker) and background (record wall) layered, with no dead central band; the speaker crisp and the chair soft

changes.problem: The records read as procedural coloured stripes, which says render more than anything else in the frame.

evidence.measured: uniform flat-colour spines, a pattern repeated cubby to cubby; clip_pct 1.45, p95 217

change.setting: record sleeve material and fill (the record wall's contents, not its design)
change.from: flat-colour spines at a single thickness, packed evenly
change.to: spine textures from a set of at least 200 real sleeve designs with printed titles, card grain, worn corners and 5-15% desaturation; thickness varied 3-6 mm (gatefolds); in each cubby a few records leaning 5-12 deg, one or two part-pulled 20-40 mm, and some cubbies 70% full

changes.expected: the wall reads as a real collection with visible print detail and irregular rhythm; no repeated stripe sequence

changes.problem: The record wall is brighter and more saturated than the product, so it competes with the hero.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 216.9 and clip 1.45% against the speaker body's p95 164

change.setting: lamps: the record wall 3 x spot
change.to: 16.0 W, cone 35 deg (softer pools that grade down the wall)

changes.expected: the record wall settles back one stop below the speaker; the speaker becomes the brightest coloured element

changes.problem: The horn is underlit and dissolves into the wall, so the product's silhouette reads only from the cabinet down.

evidence.measured: lum_median 34.0 and p95 51.6 inside the horn, against wall pixels of about 65 around it; little edge separation

change.setting: lamps: the wash behind each pair 4 x spot
change.to: 150.0 W, cone 40 deg, aimed at the wall 0.3 m above the horn's top edge so the horn is backlit and its tinted rim glows; raise the corner speaker area lamps from 10.0 to 14.0 W/m2

changes.expected: a lit halo on the wall behind the horn, the horn's tinted acrylic edge lit, and the horn's interior showing ice blue

changes.problem: The speaker's cyan light does not reach the floor or the plinth, so it does not belong to the room.

evidence.measured: floor next to the plinth r 103, g 93, b 73, with no blue lift; plinth top lum_median 26 with no cyan edge

change.to: honed dark concrete, roughness 0.35 with a roughness map from 0.25 to 0.5, base about 15% darker, so it picks up a soft cyan reflection and spill from the cabinet; give the plinth a satin top at roughness 0.3 to catch the cabinet's glow along its edge

changes.expected: a soft cyan pool on the floor at the plinth's left and front, and a thin cyan line on the plinth's top edge

changes.problem: The floor and walls are smooth CG planes without micro-detail.

change.from: smooth plaster wall; flat concrete with sparse speckle
change.to: lime plaster with a 2-4% luminance mottle at 0.3-1 m scale and a faint bump; concrete with fine aggregate, trowel arcs and a few hairline cracks at true scale (4096 px texture over at most 2 m)

changes.expected: surfaces with visible but quiet texture at full size, no tiling

changes.problem: The room lacks air and depth between the planes; the empty right corner reads as a studio sweep.

evidence.measured: smooth gradient, lum_median 62.8, range 61, no features

change.to: density 0.02, anisotropy 0.45, so the wash and record-wall spot cones read faintly in the air; add a small prop in the corner (a low side table with a rocks glass) to anchor the space

changes.expected: faint visible light cones, a gentle lift of the blacks in the distance, and the corner reading as part of a room

changes.problem: The grade is a muddy olive-brown that dulls both the wood and the speaker's ice blue.

evidence.measured: wall r 74, g 64, b 46: a greenish-amber cast

changes.expected: warm but cleaner neutrals; the wood reads as walnut, not olive; the cyan stays true

out_of_scope.request: Align the record wall's shelf heights across columns (they step between columns)
out_of_scope.why: The record wall's design is fixed; if the stepping is unintended it is a model or design question for the owner, not a picture fix

out_of_scope.request: Make the inner batts glow with more falloff through the acrylic, less evenly emissive
out_of_scope.why: This touches the speaker's materials and parts, which are fixed
